generic_mechanisms.description: Fusion/ranking can discard source-version-compatible, obligation-bearing code chunks already recalled near the top of a channel, while less sufficient evidence survives to answer generation. The resulting missing support produces a safe but false insufficient response under the current completeness contract.
generic_mechanisms.minimal_repair_seam_for_later_design: Candidate retention and ranking at the R2 channel-to-fused boundary; preserve relevance and source/version/admission safety without case-specific rules.
generic_mechanisms.opposing_safety_contract: Existing G4 T0 should-answer and must-abstain paired controls guard against relaxing G1/G2 completeness, unsupported claims, admission/provenance, or version constraints; an R2-specific generic control would be specified in a separately authorized repair design.

generic_mechanisms.description: A question-grounded bare-class premise guard can mistake an external component name for an unavailable code class and refuse despite relevant locked evidence.
generic_mechanisms.minimal_repair_seam_for_later_design: Premise classification in the existing sufficiency guard, if later generic replication justifies it.

review_limitations: The six cases are exposed and selected on insufficient_evidence; counts are not a novel_dev population rate or independent confirmation.
n001 has a locked-source versus reviewed-Gold shell-behavior conflict; no Gold record was changed, and formal Gold-scored interpretation needs forward-only review.
n010 and n019 remain causally unresolved because earlier Q1/Q2 effects cannot be excluded from observed retrieval-stage loss.
Exact finalization branch identity is not persisted, but no case requires it to establish the reported upstream R2 mechanism.
No independent second human reviewer, matched controls, fresh Lane B cohort, new QA/retrieval run, or product repair is included.
